library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2023_amisulpride"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2023_amisulpride"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2023.1215065> (open access)

Li 2023 developed a one-compartment population PK model for oral amisulpride
from routine therapeutic-drug-monitoring (TDM) samples in Chinese adults with
schizophrenia, with renal function built into the structural model a priori,
and externally validated it on a separate cohort. The model is then used to
simulate six common twice-daily regimens at three levels of renal function
(Figure 6) and the effect of eGFR on steady-state exposure (Figure 4). Both
analyses are reproduced below.

# Population

The model was fitted to the development cohort of 776 patients (on average 3
random TDM samples each) treated at Beijing Anding Hospital between December
2018 and March 2022; a further 145 patients admitted before 15 November 2019
formed the external validation cohort (Li 2023 Table 1). In the development
cohort the median age was 33 years (IQR 23-47), median weight 66 kg (IQR
57-79), 61.2% were female and 96.4% were Han Chinese. Renal function was
mostly normal or supranormal: CKD-EPI eGFR (no race component) median 114
(IQR 101-130) mL/min/1.73 m^2, 89.0% CKD stage G1, 25.4% above 130
mL/min/1.73 m^2 and only five patients in stage G3a. Daily doses averaged
566 +/- 264 mg (median 575); 12.4% of patients also received lithium.

```{r population}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2023_amisulpride"))$population
str(pop[c("n_subjects", "age_range", "weight_range", "dose_range", "renal_function")])
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Li_2023_amisulpride.R`; the table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Structure: 1 compartment, first-order absorption, linear elimination | n/a | Results 3.2; Supplementary Table S2 (model 9 'Ami final'); Supplementary Figure S6 (`ADVAN2 TRANS2`) |
| `lka` (Ka) | 0.106 1/h | Table 2, RSE 12%; bootstrap 0.106 [0.0916-0.1210] |
| `lcl` (CL/F) | 60.5 L/h | Table 2, RSE 2%; bootstrap 60.4 [58.62-62.37] |
| `lvc` (V/F) | 645 L | Table 2, RSE 18%; bootstrap 650 [521.3-769.6] |
| `e_crcl_cl` (eGFR exponent on CL/F) | 0.817 | Table 2 row 'eGFR on CL/F RCL', RSE 10%; bootstrap 0.821 [0.7030-0.9319] |
| `CL/F = 60.5 * (eGFR/113.84)^0.817` | centring 113.84 | Table 2 footnote equation; Supplementary Figure S6 `TVCL = THETA(1)*(GFR_CKD/113.84)**THETA(6)` |
| eGFR definition | CKD-EPI, race-free | Table 1 footnote; Supplementary Table S1 |
| `etalcl` | `log(1 + 0.359^2)` | Table 2, IIV CL/F 35.9% CV (RSE 7%, shrinkage 20%); exponential form from Methods Eq. 1 and Supplementary Figure S6 |
| `etalvc` | `log(1 + 1.309^2)` | Table 2, IIV V/F 130.9% CV (RSE 25%, shrinkage 46%) |
| No IIV on Ka | n/a | Supplementary Figure S6 `$OMEGA ... 0 FIX; IIV KA` |
| `propSd` | 0.346 | Table 2 'Prop.RE' 34.6% (RSE 3%) |
| `addSd` | 13.7 ng/mL | Table 2 'Add.RE' 13.7 (RSE 36%) |
| Combined error on the variance scale | n/a | Supplementary Figure S6 `W = SQRT(THETA(4)**2*IPRED**2 + THETA(5)**2)` |
| `Cc = central / vc * 1000` | n/a | Supplementary Figure S6 `S2 = V/1000` (dose in mg, concentration in ng/mL) |

## The IIV scale

Table 2 prints the between-subject variability only as a percent CV, and the
paper does not say how the CV was computed. For an exponential eta the two
usual conventions are `CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)` and `CV = sqrt(omega^2)`.
They nearly agree for CL/F but not for the large V/F variability:

```{r iiv-scale}
tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c("CL/F", "V/F"),
  cv_pct = c(35.9, 130.9)
) |>
  mutate(
    omega2_exact = log(1 + (cv_pct / 100)^2),
    omega2_sqrt = (cv_pct / 100)^2
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter,
    "Published CV (%)" = cv_pct,
    "omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) (packaged)" = omega2_exact,
    "omega^2 = CV^2 (alternative)" = omega2_sqrt
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

The control stream in Supplementary Figure S6 does not settle it: its
`$OMEGA` starting values (0.187 and 0.5) are round numbers far from either
reading, as are its `$THETA` starting values (60, 700, 0.1, 0.35, 18). The
maintainers therefore used `log(1 + CV^2)`, the convention used across this
package. The choice matters only for the spread of V/F, which in a model with
slow absorption (Ka 0.106 1/h) affects mainly the within-interval fluctuation;
the [TDM cohort check](#tdm-cohort-check) below shows that the observed
dose-normalised concentration distribution cannot tell the two readings apart.

# Figure 6: six regimens at three levels of renal function

Li 2023 simulated each regimen for 8 days (morning dose at 0 h every 24 h,
evening dose at 12 h every 24 h) and plotted the last 24 h (144-168 h) at
eGFR 50, 100 and 200 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (Supplementary Figure S7). The
simulation below follows that design with 100 virtual subjects per regimen and
eGFR level, sampling IIV on CL/F and V/F.

```{r regimens}
regimens <- tibble::tibble(
  regimen = c(
    "100 mg + 100 mg", "100 mg + 200 mg", "200 mg + 200 mg",
    "200 mg + 400 mg", "400 mg + 400 mg", "600 mg + 600 mg"
  ),
  dose_am = c(100, 100, 200, 200, 400, 600),
  dose_pm = c(100, 200, 200, 400, 400, 600)
) |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimen))

# Explicit dose rows (no addl) so the same table feeds rxSolve and PKNCA.
make_events <- function(subj, obs_times, last_dose = 156) {
  am <- subj |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(0, last_dose, by = 24)) |>
    mutate(amt = dose_am)
  pm <- subj |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(12, last_dose, by = 24)) |>
    mutate(amt = dose_pm)
  doses <- bind_rows(am, pm) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, CRCL, regimen, egfr_label)
}

egfr_levels <- c(50, 100, 200)
egfr_names <- c(
  "eGFR 50 (mild-to-moderate impairment)",
  "eGFR 100 (normal)",
  "eGFR 200 (hyperfiltration)"
)
n_per_cell <- 100L

subj_fig6 <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  regimens,
  CRCL = egfr_levels,
  rep = seq_len(n_per_cell)
) |>
  mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    egfr_label = factor(egfr_names[match(CRCL, egfr_levels)], levels = egfr_names)
  )

obs_ss <- seq(144, 168, by = 0.5)
ev_fig6 <- make_events(subj_fig6, obs_ss)
```

```{r simulate-fig6}
mod <- readModelDb("Li_2023_amisulpride")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230915)
sim_fig6 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_fig6,
  keep = c("regimen", "egfr_label")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-6, fig.height = 8}
band_df <- tibble::tibble(
  ymin = c(50, 100, 320, 640),
  ymax = c(100, 320, 640, 5000),
  zone = c("below range", "AGNP range", "above range", "above alert level")
)

# `sim` is the simulated observation (IIV plus residual error).
fig6_q <- sim_fig6 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  group_by(egfr_label, regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    Q50 = median(sim),
    Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    ipred_Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    ipred_Q50 = median(Cc),
    ipred_Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fig6_q |>
  mutate(tss = time - 144) |>
  ggplot(aes(tss, Q50)) +
  geom_rect(
    data = band_df,
    aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = zone),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = egfr_label)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q05, colour = egfr_label), linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q95, colour = egfr_label), linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_grid(regimen ~ egfr_label) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(50, 100, 320, 640, 1000, 2000, 5000)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 6, 12, 18, 24)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "below range" = "grey60", "AGNP range" = "green3",
    "above range" = "gold", "above alert level" = "red"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = "Time at steady state (h)", y = "Amisulpride (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Li 2023: median (solid) and 5th-95th percentiles (dotted)."
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

The pattern matches Figure 6: the median sits in the AGNP range (100-320
ng/mL) for 200 mg/day at eGFR 50 and 100 and below it at eGFR 200; it crosses
the 640 ng/mL alert level at 800 mg/day only with impaired renal function.

The paper does not say whether its Figure 6 bands include residual error.
Read by eye off Figure 6B (eGFR 100), the 95th percentile is about 2.3 times
the median and the 5th percentile about 0.5 times. The upper band is
reproduced only when residual error is included, so the plot above includes
it; the lower band falls between the two versions:

```{r figure-6-bands}
fig6_q |>
  group_by(egfr_label) |>
  summarise(
    up_obs = mean(Q95 / Q50),
    lo_obs = mean(Q05 / Q50),
    up_ipred = mean(ipred_Q95 / ipred_Q50),
    lo_ipred = mean(ipred_Q05 / ipred_Q50)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Renal function" = egfr_label,
    "Q95/median, with residual" = up_obs,
    "Q05/median, with residual" = lo_obs,
    "Q95/median, IIV only" = up_ipred,
    "Q05/median, IIV only" = lo_ipred
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Band width relative to the median, averaged over regimens and times.")
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA is run on the steady-state dosing interval (144-168 h) of the typical
patient (random effects set to zero) for every regimen and eGFR level. Because
both sides use the same parameters, the average concentration must equal the
closed form `Cav = daily dose / (24 * CL/F)` up to trapezoidal error, and the
assertion is tight.

```{r typical-sim}
subj_typ <- tidyr::expand_grid(regimens, CRCL = egfr_levels) |>
  mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    egfr_label = factor(egfr_names[match(CRCL, egfr_levels)], levels = egfr_names)
  )
ev_typ <- make_events(subj_typ, obs_ss)

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = ev_typ,
  keep = c("regimen", "egfr_label")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r pknca}
conc_ss <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen, egfr_label)

dose_ss <- ev_typ |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen, egfr_label)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ss, Cc ~ time | egfr_label + regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | egfr_label + regimen + id)

intervals_ss <- data.frame(
  start = 144, end = 168,
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals_ss)
)

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  select(egfr_label, regimen, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(select(subj_typ, id, CRCL, dose_am, dose_pm), by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    cl_typ = 60.5 * (CRCL / 113.84)^0.817,
    cav_closed = (dose_am + dose_pm) / (24 * cl_typ) * 1000,
    pct_diff = 100 * (cav - cav_closed) / cav_closed
  )

nca_wide |>
  select(egfr_label, regimen, cmax, cmin, cav, cav_closed, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Renal function" = egfr_label,
    "Regimen (morning + evening)" = regimen,
    "Cmax,ss (ng/mL)" = cmax,
    "Cmin,ss (ng/mL)" = cmin,
    "Cav,ss PKNCA (ng/mL)" = cav,
    "Cav,ss closed form (ng/mL)" = cav_closed,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-patient steady-state exposure, 144-168 h.")

stopifnot(
  nrow(nca_wide) == 18L,
  # Same parameters on both sides: pure numerical (trapezoidal) error.
  all(abs(nca_wide$pct_diff) < 1)
)
```

The paper reports no NCA table, so there is no published-versus-simulated
NCA comparison. Its Results 3.5 makes several statements about the typical
patient that can be checked against the table above:

```{r results-claims}
cav_of <- function(egfr, reg) {
  nca_wide$cav[nca_wide$CRCL == egfr & nca_wide$regimen == reg]
}
claims <- tibble::tibble(
  claim = c(
    "200 mg/day, eGFR 50: within 100-320 ng/mL",
    "200 mg/day, eGFR 100: within 100-320 ng/mL",
    "200 mg/day, eGFR 200: below 100 ng/mL",
    "800 mg/day, eGFR 100: above 320 but below 640 ng/mL",
    "800 mg/day, eGFR 50: above 640 ng/mL"
  ),
  cav = c(
    cav_of(50, "100 mg + 100 mg"),
    cav_of(100, "100 mg + 100 mg"),
    cav_of(200, "100 mg + 100 mg"),
    cav_of(100, "400 mg + 400 mg"),
    cav_of(50, "400 mg + 400 mg")
  ),
  holds = c(
    cav[1] > 100 & cav[1] < 320,
    cav[2] > 100 & cav[2] < 320,
    cav[3] < 100,
    cav[4] > 320 & cav[4] < 640,
    cav[5] > 640
  )
)
claims |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Li 2023 Results 3.5 statement (typical patient)" = claim,
    "Simulated Cav,ss (ng/mL)" = cav,
    "Holds" = holds
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0)
stopifnot(all(claims$holds))
```

# Figure 4: eGFR effect on steady-state exposure

Figure 4 shows the ratio of steady-state AUC, Cmax and Cmin at eGFR 30-200
mL/min/1.73 m^2 to the reference eGFR of 110 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Because the
model is linear, the AUC ratio is exactly `(eGFR / 110)^-0.817`; Cmax and Cmin
ratios differ slightly because the elimination rate, and with it the
within-interval shape, changes with eGFR. The figure's medians are read by eye
off its log axis (about +/- 5%).

```{r figure-4}
egfr_forest <- c(30, 60, 90, 110, 120, 150, 200)
subj_forest <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_along(egfr_forest),
  CRCL = egfr_forest,
  dose_am = 200, dose_pm = 200,
  regimen = "200 mg + 200 mg",
  egfr_label = paste("eGFR", egfr_forest)
)
ev_forest <- make_events(subj_forest, obs_ss)
sim_forest <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = ev_forest,
  keep = c("regimen", "egfr_label")
) |>
  as.data.frame()

nca_forest <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    filter(sim_forest, !is.na(Cc)) |> select(id, time, Cc, egfr_label),
    Cc ~ time | egfr_label + id
  ),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
    filter(ev_forest, evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, egfr_label),
    amt ~ time | egfr_label + id
  ),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 144, end = 168, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
))

forest <- as.data.frame(nca_forest$result) |>
  select(id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(select(subj_forest, id, CRCL), by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    auc_ratio = auclast / auclast[CRCL == 110],
    cmax_ratio = cmax / cmax[CRCL == 110],
    cmin_ratio = cmin / cmin[CRCL == 110],
    auc_closed = (CRCL / 110)^-0.817
  ) |>
  filter(CRCL != 110) |>
  arrange(CRCL) |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      CRCL = c(30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 200),
      fig4_auc = c(2.9, 1.65, 1.2, 0.95, 0.79, 0.61)
    ),
    by = "CRCL"
  )

forest |>
  select(CRCL, auc_ratio, auc_closed, fig4_auc, cmax_ratio, cmin_ratio) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)" = CRCL,
    "AUCss ratio (simulated)" = auc_ratio,
    "AUCss ratio (closed form)" = auc_closed,
    "AUCss ratio (Figure 4, by eye)" = fig4_auc,
    "Cmax,ss ratio" = cmax_ratio,
    "Cmin,ss ratio" = cmin_ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Exposure relative to eGFR 110 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (typical patient, 200 mg twice daily).")

stopifnot(
  # Linear model: simulated and closed-form AUC ratios share all parameters.
  # 2%, not tighter: at eGFR 30 the half-life is about 21 h, so the 144 h
  # run-in reaches only about 99% of steady state.
  all(abs(forest$auc_ratio / forest$auc_closed - 1) < 0.02),
  # Against the by-eye reading of Figure 4.
  all(abs(forest$auc_ratio / forest$fig4_auc - 1) < 0.10)
)

forest |>
  select(CRCL, auc_ratio, cmax_ratio, cmin_ratio) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-CRCL, names_to = "metric", values_to = "ratio") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(
    metric,
    levels = c("auc_ratio", "cmax_ratio", "cmin_ratio"),
    labels = c("AUCss", "Cmax,ss", "Cmin,ss")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(ratio, factor(paste("eGFR =", CRCL), levels = paste("eGFR =", c(30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 200))))) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.8, xmax = 1.25, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(colour = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~metric) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.5, 0.8, 1.25, 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Ratio to eGFR 110 mL/min/1.73 m^2", y = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the medians of Figure 4 of Li 2023 (typical patient)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# TDM cohort check

Li 2023 Table 1 reports the development-cohort amisulpride concentration
normalised by daily dose: median 0.67 ng/mL per mg (IQR 0.428-0.946). A
virtual TDM cohort is built from the Table 1 covariate summaries and sampled
once per subject at a random time within a twice-daily dosing interval after
two weeks of dosing, with residual error included:

* eGFR log-normal with median 114 and the log-scale SD implied by the IQR
  101-130, truncated to 40-200 mL/min/1.73 m^2;
* daily dose normal with mean 566 and SD 264 mg (Table 1), truncated to the
  100-1190 mg range of the development cohort and rounded to 50 mg, split into
  two equal doses (the per-patient regimen is not reported).

The same cohort is solved under both IIV readings from the
[IIV scale](#the-iiv-scale) section.

```{r tdm-cohort}
set.seed(20230916)
n_tdm <- 200L
egfr_sdlog <- (log(130) - log(101)) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))
subj_tdm <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_tdm),
  CRCL = pmin(pmax(114 * exp(rnorm(n_tdm, 0, egfr_sdlog)), 40), 200),
  daily = round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_tdm, 566, 264), 100), 1190) / 50) * 50,
  t_obs = 336 + runif(n_tdm, 0, 12)
) |>
  mutate(
    dose_am = daily / 2, dose_pm = daily / 2,
    regimen = "TDM", egfr_label = "TDM"
  )

# Doses to 336 h, then one observation per subject at its own time.
ev_tdm <- bind_rows(
  make_events(subj_tdm, numeric(0), last_dose = 336),
  subj_tdm |>
    transmute(
      id, time = t_obs, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central",
      CRCL, regimen, egfr_label
    )
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

# omega^2 = CV^2: 0.359^2 and 1.309^2
mod_alt <- mod |>
  rxode2::ini(etalcl ~ 0.128881, etalvc ~ 1.713481)

solve_tdm <- function(m, seed) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(seed)
  rxode2::rxSolve(m, events = ev_tdm) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    select(id, sim) |>
    left_join(select(subj_tdm, id, daily), by = "id") |>
    mutate(cd = sim / daily)
}
tdm_pack <- solve_tdm(mod, 20230917)
tdm_alt <- solve_tdm(mod_alt, 20230917)

tdm_sum <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(source = "Li 2023 Table 1 (observed)", q25 = 0.428, q50 = 0.67, q75 = 0.946),
  tdm_pack |> summarise(q25 = quantile(cd, 0.25), q50 = median(cd), q75 = quantile(cd, 0.75)) |>
    mutate(source = "Simulated, omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) (packaged)"),
  tdm_alt |> summarise(q25 = quantile(cd, 0.25), q50 = median(cd), q75 = quantile(cd, 0.75)) |>
    mutate(source = "Simulated, omega^2 = CV^2")
) |>
  select(source, q25, q50, q75)

tdm_sum |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Source" = source,
    "25th percentile" = q25,
    "Median" = q50,
    "75th percentile" = q75
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Dose-normalised concentration (ng/mL per mg daily dose).")

stopifnot(
  # The centre is set by CL/F alone (1000 / (24 * 60.5) = 0.69 at the
  # reference eGFR); a wrong CL/F, unit or exponent moves it by tens of percent.
  abs(tdm_sum$q50[2] / 0.67 - 1) < 0.15
)
```

The simulated median matches the observed 0.67 ng/mL per mg. The simulated IQR
is a little narrower at the lower end than the observed one, which is expected
given that the virtual cohort has no once-daily or unequal split regimens and
no non-adherence. The two IIV readings give nearly the same distribution,
which is why this check cannot choose between them.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV as %CV only. The maintainers converted
  with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`; the alternative `omega^2 = CV^2` gives a
  V/F variance of 1.71 instead of 1.00. See [The IIV scale](#the-iiv-scale).
* **No IIV on Ka.** The control stream (Supplementary Figure S6) carries an
  `ETA(3)` on Ka with variance `0 FIX`, i.e. no variability; it is omitted.
* **Centring value.** The eGFR reference is 113.84 mL/min/1.73 m^2 as printed
  in the Table 2 equation and the control stream. (A later summary of this
  model in Yan 2024, doi:10.2147/DDDT.S469149, prints 113.87.)
* **Figure 6 dosing.** The simulation follows the R code of Supplementary
  Figure S7 (morning dose at 0 h and evening dose at 12 h, every 24 h, plotted
  over 144-168 h). That code samples no random effects, but Figure 6 shows
  percentile bands, so IIV on CL/F and V/F and residual error are sampled
  here (the band-width table above shows why residual error is included).
  The paper simulated 500 subjects per regimen; 100 per regimen and eGFR
  level are used here.
* **Results 3.5 versus Figure 6.** The text states that at 1200 mg/day "all
  patients regardless of their renal function would have exceeded the
  laboratory alert threshold", but in Figure 6C (eGFR 200) the 600 mg + 600 mg
  median lies below 640 ng/mL, as it does here (typical Cav about 520 ng/mL).
  The figure is consistent with the model; the sentence is not checked.
* **Virtual TDM cohort.** The per-patient dose regimen, sampling times and
  eGFR distribution are not published; the cohort above is built from the
  Table 1 summaries with the stated assumptions (twice-daily equal doses,
  random sampling time, log-normal eGFR).
* **Table 1 inconsistencies.** The Table 1 dose range columns
  (development 100-1190 mg, validation 50-1220 mg) are swapped relative to
  Results 3.1 (development 50-1220 mg, validation 100-1190 mg), and the
  Results text gives the validation cohort as 38.8% female while Table 1 gives
  47.6%. Neither affects the model.
* No correction notice for Li 2023 was found (literature check 2026-10-27).
